summary: OPTIMISM (Operational Planetary Telemetry & Interactive Mission Simulation) is a browser-based junior astronaut mission trainer built for learners ages 7–12. Unlike conventional space games that feature instant controls, OPTIMISM challenges players to act as NASA Mission Control Flight Directors who must outsmart real speed-of-light radio latency (2.6 seconds round-trip between Earth and the Moon) to guide an Artemis astronaut safely across Shackleton Crater. Grounded in NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) topographic slope and illumination parameters alongside NASA DONKI space weather dynamics, players build predictive command queues to extract lunar ice cores while surviving -180°C Permanently Shadowed Regions and sudden solar flares.By turning real orbital physics, thermal management, and telemetry queuing into tactile, cause-and-effect gameplay, OPTIMISM bridges the gap between overly simplified space trivia and complex aerospace engineering—empowering the next generation of explorers to think like real NASA flight controllers.
details:
• What it does & How it works: OPTIMISM (Operational Planetary Telemetry & Interactive Mission Simulation) is an immersive, browser-based junior astronaut mission trainer designed for learners ages 7–12. Unlike conventional space games that feature instant controls, OPTIMISM forces players to act as NASA Mission Control Flight Directors who must manage real speed-of-light radio latency (a 1.5 to 3.5-second signal delay between Earth and the Moon). Players queue predictive command sequences (Movement, Core Drilling, Thermal Heater Boost, and Radiation Shielding) on an 8x8 lunar grid to extract ice cores from Shackleton Crater and return safely to the Artemis lander.
  • Benefits & Intended Impact: The project bridges the gap between over-simplified space trivia and dense aerospace engineering. It teaches children foundational STEM concepts—such as telemetry queuing, thermal survival in $-180^\circ\text{C}$ Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs), and orbital light-speed propagation—through tactile, high-stakes arcade gameplay.
  • Tools, Tech Stack & Software: Built as a single-page web application using Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, and Lucide Icons. It incorporates the browser-native Web Audio API for real-time synthesized NASA telemetry sound effects and the Web Speech API (webkitSpeechRecognition) to allow voice-activated Mission Control commands ("🎙️ Mic Comms").
  • Creativity & NASA Data Integration: OPTIMISM is grounded in authentic scientific parameters, utilizing NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA elevation and illumination data (topographic slopes and crater shadows) alongside NASA DONKI space weather telemetry (simulating Coronal Mass Ejections that require timely radiation shielding).
  • Design Considerations: To ensure a seamless user experience, the team engineered a strict state-machine architecture to prevent race conditions during signal transmissions, implemented hardcoded solvable maps to avoid softlocks, and designed a dense single-screen cockpit with a "Junior Mode" hint toggle for accessible play.
